questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to an english-speaking country and thought that would also be a good opportunity to further my legal english vocabulary.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Not a 10, because some of the information from our host university was not consistent with what we were told when we arrived at our exchange university.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy, but as mentioned, some of the information we got from QMUL was not consistent with what we were told back at our host-university or what was stated in the information pamphlet.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We were given the opportunity to speak with the Global Opportunities office during orientation week, which was nice.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Not easy at all. Everything was very expensive, especially when searching for only yourself. There might have been more options if you were a larger group searching.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's really expensive and you should start searching early.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy as we got a link from our home institution and just had to fill out the information. After that we received a registration number which we used when registering for classes and so on.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: We could ask our home institution if anything was unclear, and we had also received an email-address for the contact person at our host university.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got almost all the classes I initially registered for. One of them was not created so I was given one of the alternatives I listed.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The options available for exchange students are quite slim, so be prepared to take classes you don't necessarily find super interesting.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The academics were quite different from what we're used to and not all the professors were aware of, for example, that there were different exams for exchange and full year students.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The levels of the courses were quite different. I had one first year (level 4) course, while others were level 6 and intended for second year students. The courses were very different in nature so the level of them are not very comparable.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Similar in some ways and very different in others. At Queen Mary the tutorials and seminars were much more discussion based, while the style of teaching at UCPH is more of a run-through of the curriculum with time for questions and discussions if anything is unclear.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Contract Law - Competition Law - Democracy and Justice - Law, Knowledge, Power

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Competition Law was very informative and useful for out further studies at UCPH.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Transportation was a bit more expensive than expected.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries were more expensive than expected, but it was not surprising with the general rise in prices.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Various sorts of sports; football, swimming, running, climbing etc. The clubs organised social gatherings with the members.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The sports clubs are nice if you want to try a new sport or have a interest in one already, but I didn't do any clubs so I wouldn't know what to recommend.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: There are many opportunities to do day trips or weekend trips to, for example, Bath, Oxford or Cambridge. The different markets in London are also very fun to visit on weekends.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy as England is not that different from what we're used to and I had visited London many times before, but it did take some time to adjust to the different style of teaching and university experience in general.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Everyone I talked to was very friendly and willing to help answer any question you might have about the university or school. I'd recommend just talking to people in class or at the campus cafés, everybody's really friendly.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The difference I found the most difficult was more academic as it took me a bit of time to adjust to learning about law in a common law system as opposed to a civil law system.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People are much more likely to come up and talk to you in class, restaurants and bars, which I only thought was a fun thing.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1) Search for housing in good time, 2) be prepared for a limited choice of classes, 3) the teachers expect a lot more participation through discussions in seminar-based classes.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The coffee at the Grond Cafe is better than at the small Starbucks at The Curve ;)

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new people and getting out of my comfort zone having to adjust to a whole new everyday life in a new city.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Not seeing my family and friends for such a long period of time.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Exchange is nerve-racking, but it's an experience of a life time. If you are considering it, go for it.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
